title: Global sections are invariants in a canonical abelian geometric stalk equivalence
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-pc-field-extension], $K^s$ a separable closure [def-pd-separable-closure], and $\Omega$ an algebraically closed algebraic extension of $K$ containing $K^s$ in a compatible algebra tower. Let $S=\operatorname{Spec}K$, $G=\operatorname{Gal}(K^s/K)$ with its Krull topology, and $p$ the geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. Let $E:\operatorname{Sh}(S_{\mathrm{et}},\mathrm{Ab}_{u+1})\simeq\operatorname{DiscreteRep}_{\mathbf Z}(G)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-exc-discrete-modules-category] be an equivalence equipped with a natural additive identification $i$ of its underlying groups with the geometric stalk [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Assume its action on germs is given by changing lifts: whenever $\tau\in\operatorname{Aut}_K(\Omega)$ restricts to $g\in G$ and $x\prime=\operatorname{Spec}(\tau)\circ x$, $i(g\cdot i^{-1}(\operatorname{germ}_x z))=\operatorname{germ}_{x\prime}z$. Then evaluation at the terminal etale object is naturally isomorphic to $F\mapsto E(F)^G$, with the latter maps the restrictions of equivariant coefficient maps.

proof.text: Apply the existing sections/stalk-invariants theorem to the underlying set sheaf. The forgetful functor commutes with the stalk and germ maps. Represent each germ and compare its two actions using an extending automorphism and the point action; they agree.

Specialize to the bottom intermediate field. Its fixing subgroup is all of G. The spectrum of the bottom field is isomorphic to the terminal etale object using botEquiv. Naturality of germs transports the bijection to global sections. The terminal germ followed by i inverse is additive, invariant, and bijective onto the invariant subgroup. Its naturality follows from naturality of the terminal germ transformation and i inverse. Form the natural isomorphism from these bijective components.
